title: Weekly Update - New Quests, Activities, Upcoming Patches & More Coming Soon! - RuneScape Dragonwilds
author: IAmWaved
description:
This weekly episode for #runescapedragonwilds covers the upcoming update arriving sometime this week, bringing new quests, activities and quality of life, as well as plenty of bug fixes, balancing and more!

We also touch on the upcoming Luminance update this December, any recently known issues, and the 2027 roadmap.

Comment below with ideas and enthusiasm (if you have any) for any Dragonwilds Community videos, like arena fighting, hide & seek, among us etc. and I'll have plenty more details soon!

transcript.text: Hello folks, we do have some incredibly exciting news for RuneScape Dragon Wilds today as in a recent comment the devs
revealed an upcoming patch for sometime this week including new content like a quest line and activities, but also
addressing things like stamina regen, delayed switching, the spell wheel overlay, and much more. Alongside this,
we have comments regarding hot fixes being slowed down so as to avoid game-breaking issues. We have a current
overview of what issues are affecting the game right now, and then a few details regarding what we can expect for
the end of the year and then beginning of next as we move into 2027's Blood Crystal Saga. As a quick side note,
right at the very end, I'll be discussing some ideas I have for some community competitions, events, and
whatnot on my own private Dragon Wilds servers. It's a work in progress and something I'll be discussing more as
time goes on, but if that sounds interesting to yourself, then stick around at the end and I'll share more
details then. Anyway, plenty for us to get through and as usual, we are not wasting any time, so let's get started.
Okay, so the first thing I wanted to touch on for today would be the upcoming update. This was first mentioned in a
recent comment by Mod Doom where he basically asked for more info on a known issue, revealed that November's update
is being worked on right now, and that they are reducing the number of hot fixes they deploy due to the limitations
they place on crossplay. Player feedback has been very clear on this topic. With that in mind, they're focusing their
attention on larger fixes tied to the regular monthly updates to minimize disruption unless it is absolutely
necessary. A few days after this, we actually received a few more details regarding the update itself and so that
comment goes as follows. Hey, we've got a patch releasing next week at the time of writing with a pretty extensive list
of fixes. I should wait until next week to share a full write-up and a bit more of an overview on where we are, but just
so this doesn't sit here with no response until then, the patch is including fixes for: doors looking funky
on multiplayer worlds, spell wheel overlay bugs, delayed switching, stamina regen, and then music bugs. A known
issue on dedicated servers where player-built structures lose collision after long periods of time, and then a
bunch more I won't fully copy out here, but rest assured we're on the case with a lot of these. We're also adding more
content including a new quest and activities. Our 1.0 release was a cohesive saga now playable on consoles,
but realistically we're distinguishing ourselves from other survival games whose 1.0 release was quote and quote
the end. We're continuing to iterate and polish, but we've also got an expansive road map of content for years to come.
It's a balance of polishing as we go, but also continually growing the game. Now, the biggest couple of takeaways
here for myself would be that hot fixes are being toned down, which I think is a very solid move. Whilst I like the idea
of the game constantly being tweaked for the better, what's actually been happening as a result of the snappy hot
fixes is that they fix a bunch, but then break other things. And since the console launch we've kind of just had a
revolving door of both minor and major issues affecting players across the board. Hopefully now with less hot fixes
and more time spent testing the changes themselves before they go live, we should see fewer problems moving
forward, but I would imagine we will still see the odd issue here or there too, as these things won't be 100%
avoidable. Anyway, the second takeaway then would be the arrival of the next update itself. It's said to have a new
quest line and new activities as well as fixes and tweaks to things like stamina
region, delayed switching, and the spell wheel overlay bug. But then I'm sure there's some other more exciting stuff
within here that we don't currently know about just yet. Like how last month's update had new special attacks for
ranged weapons, separate slots for both rings and amulets, and even a jumping attack amongst various other things. We
are on Tuesday already, which leaves just six or so days for this update to arrive. It could of course still yet be
delayed, but just going off the last comment by Mac Doom, we can expect this sometime over the next few days now. And
so, as soon as it arrives, I will of course be covering it all right here in full.
Now, the next thing I want to touch on for today would be the current known issues. Previously we've had cross play
issues, character saves being lost, world progression being lost, and a few other biggies here and there too.
However, I'm quite pleased to be saying that as of right now it appears that most if not all game breaking issues
have seemingly been resolved. Bar at least one that seems to be affecting a few folks, and that would be that some
players aren't able to join worlds with any more than two players present already. Whether the error message be
cannot join with this character type, network connection interrupted, or whatever else. This is absolutely a
known issue, and as of today is being investigated further by the devs. I've no idea how widespread this issue
actually is. Hopefully though, not much at all, but it's likely we'll hear more about this moving forward, and possibly
even receive a fix for it within this upcoming update. But then, even if we don't, rest assured it's on their radar,
and so just like everything else, will be ironed out eventually. Aside from this though, there doesn't appear to be
any other issues right now, or at least not any massive or widespread ones like there have been recently. And so,
fingers crossed this continues to be the case now that hot fixes are being slowed
down, and updates are being fleshed out more before they arrive. I won't hold my breath too much though, as really
anything can happen, and so we will just have to wait and see. Now, of course, beyond any updates we receive this
month, we are steadily getting ever closer to the big Lumina's content update arriving in December, which we
already know brings all manner of new content with it, like the Pyre skill, fairy rings, musical instruments,
musical puzzles, new equipment, lands, enemies, quest lines, and more. I have broken this down already, so go check
out this video right here if you would like the full scoop. But otherwise, we've no idea when in December this will
all arrive. But it does mark the very last update that Coelus Saga receives, marking the end of the game's first full
saga and then leaving the door wide open for the Blood Crystal Saga in 2027, which we'll circle back to and cover
very shortly. Luminants will be the first official large content update that console players will receive, if we
disregard all of the new content added in with the console launch, as from a console player's perspective, like
myself, all of that stuff has been in the game since day one. This makes the upcoming update pretty exciting, as I
haven't even been able to get through half of the currently available content in the past month or so already. I feel
like I've played a ton, but in the grand scheme of things, I haven't been playing
this game very long at all, and it's now already receiving a major content update. By the time I do get through
what content is still left, and then what's added in with this new update, we'll either be coming up on the next
major content update for March 2027 or have already passed it, by which point we then begin moving into June's major
content update, and so on and so forth. Put simply, the entirety of 2027 will be
broken up into 12 major updates, four of which will be much bigger and contain a ton more content than the others. Those
four being the March, June, September and then December updates. And then the other eight spread in between will be
very similar to both the recent October and coming November updates in that they
include a range of stuff like quality of life, new content, bug fixes, balancing,
etc. Four new skills have been confirmed for 2027 as well. We have Hunter arriving in March and then Slayer
arriving in December. However, we've no idea what the other two skills could be right now. Alongside this, all four
updates will pertain to a new overarching story involving elves and vampires and we can expect all manner of
new and exciting stuff, whether it be new maps, enemies, equipment, mounts, building kits, etc. I do have a video
touching on what we know of the 2027 road map already, and it's likely I'll cover it again in the future once more
is revealed. But the general sentiment is that we have a very long and exciting road ahead of us, and the current
timeline from September's console release up to December's first major content update will paint a very good
example as to what we can expect for Dragon Wilds for years to come. Naturally, as and when all future
developments are revealed, I will be dropping future news videos covering all topics as I have done for the past
couple of months already. However, just recently I've been looking into other ways of covering Dragon Wilds given it
is a unique experience with very close-knit team-driven mechanics. And so, after doing some digging into
private servers and hosting my own private events or competitions, it is now something I'm really keen on
eventually doing. I'm not entirely sure what the exact specifics would be, but I'm imagining things like 10 to 15
player events, games and competitions, similar to say Among Us, arena fights, hide and seek, etc. And then
theoretically, I would turn all of these into episodes for the channel, creating somewhat of an ongoing series. I'm I'm
entirely sure if this is a good idea as it could end up being a complete waste of time and a great deal of effort for
very little payoff. But, I'd like to try new things and I'm keen on this specific idea. So, at the very least, I'm going
to give it a go before writing it off entirely. Let me know below if you'd be interested in taking part in any such
events. This won't guarantee you a position at all, as once I finally fleshed things out further, I'll be
making multiple announcements for recruitment and other things. But, at the very least, I do want to get the
feelers out there, get an idea on general consensus, and maybe get a few ideas from yourselves along the way,
too. Feel free to comment below and keep an eye out for future Dragon Wilds posts and videos, as there will routinely be
more information regarding all of this within those videos. Anyway, aside from all of that, and of course the guarantee
of more news videos just as and when more updates arrive, this is all basically just to say that do feel free
to treat this channel as your one-stop spot for all things RuneScape Dragon Wilds moving forward. That would be it
for this one, folks. I'll be back soon with plenty more, and I do of course have a range of guide and news videos on
the channel already, so do feel free to stop on by and check things out. Otherwise, thanks for watching, folks,
and until next time. Peace.
